words.ex: It rained; hence, the game was canceled.
use: The demand rose; hence the higher price.
He's new here, hence all the questions.
mcq: The flight was delayed; hence, we missed the meeting.
The flight delayed hence so we missed it.
Hence the flight, we missed the meeting because.
We missed hence because the flight.
words.note: hence = 그래서(격식). 'hence + 명사'로 동사 없이도 써요!

words.ex: I don't drink coffee anymore.
use: 우리는 더 이상 거기 안 살아요.
mcq: I don't use that app anymore.
I don't use that app no more anymore.
Anymore I don't use that app not.
words.note: anymore는 부정문과 짝! 긍정문에는 still을 써요.

words.ex: Initially, I didn't like the idea.
use: The project was initially planned for March.
Initially free, the app now charges a fee.
mcq: The plan initially was seeming perfect at first beginning.
At initially the plan was perfect.
words.note: initially(부사) = at first. initial은 형용사!

words.ex: I occasionally work from home.
use: We occasionally eat out on weekends.
Occasionally, the system needs a restart.
mcq: I occasionally check my old emails.
I occasional check my old emails.
I check occasionally sometimes my emails.
words.note: occasionally = sometimes보다 빈도 낮음. occasional(형용사)과 구분!

words.ex: Music is a universal language.
use: The charger has a universal plug.
그 충전기는 만능 플러그가 달려 있다.
There was universal agreement on the plan.
words.note: universal(형용사) = 어디에나 적용되는. universally는 부사!

words.ex: The update was installed successfully.
use: We successfully launched the new service.
mcq: He success passed the exam fully.
words.note: successfully(부사)가 동사를 꾸며요. successful은 형용사!

words.ex: She's a champion of small businesses.
use: He championed the new policy from day one.
그는 첫날부터 그 정책을 강력히 지지했다.
mcq: She championed for the campaign to.
words.note: champion을 동사로! = 앞장서서 지지하다. 뜻밖의 고급 용법이에요.

words.ex: That was a wise decision.
use: It's wise to save before spending.
My grandmother gave me wise advice.
mcq: It would be wise to wait.
It would be wisely to wait.
Waiting is wise to be it.
To wait wise would be it.
words.note: It is wise to + 동사 = ~하는 게 현명하다. 조언할 때 유용한 틀!

words.ex: They made an amendment to the contract.
use: The amendment takes effect next month.
Small amendments improved the proposal a lot.
mcq: We proposed an amendment to the rules.
We proposed an amendment of to the rules.
We amended an amendment the rules.
words.note: amendment to + 문서. amend(동사)의 명사형!

words.ex: The country faces economic sanctions.
words.exko: 그 나라는 경제 제재를 받고 있어요.
use: New sanctions were imposed last week.
The plan was sanctioned by the board.
mcq: Sanctions were imposed on the company.
Sanctions were imposed to the company.
words.note: impose sanctions on = ~에 제재를 가하다. 뉴스 필수 단어!

words.ex: Her parents were immigrants from Vietnam.
use: The city has a large immigrant community.
그 도시엔 큰 이민자 커뮤니티가 있다.
Many immigrants start their own businesses.
mcq: He immigrants from his country first.
words.note: immigrant(사람) vs immigration(제도·이민 자체) vs immigrate(동사) 구분!

words.ex: Please follow the safety guidelines.
use: The new guidelines take effect Monday.
We set clear guidelines for remote work.
words.note: 보통 복수 guidelines로 써요. follow/set guidelines가 기본 짝!

words.ex: A cluster of shops opened near the station.
use: The tech cluster attracts young talent.
그 테크 단지는 젊은 인재를 끌어들인다.
mcq: People clustered at around to the screen.
words.note: cluster around = ~주위에 모이다. 명사·동사 둘 다!

words.ex: My phone is out of storage.
use: We rented a storage unit for our furniture.
Cloud storage makes file sharing easy.
클라우드 저장소 덕에 파일 공유가 쉽다.
mcq: I need more storage on my laptop.
I need more storages on my laptop.
I need storage more in laptop many.
words.note: storage는 셀 수 없는 명사! 복수형 없어요.

words.ex: We need a more flexible plan.
use: My hours are flexible on Fridays.
words.note: flexible about + 대상. 일정 조율의 마법 단어!

words.ex: She trains like a professional athlete.
use: The athletes arrived for the tournament.
He was a natural athlete in school.
mcq: He's the best athlete on the team.
He's the best athletic on the team.
He athletes best on the team.
words.note: athlete(선수·명사) vs athletic(운동 잘하는·형용사) 구분!

words.ex: The color faded after many washes.
mcq: The jeans faded away over time going.
The jeans made fade over time.
words.note: fade = 서서히 옅어지다. fade out(점점 사라지다)도 함께!

words.ex: The book is on the top shelf.
words.exko: 그 책은 맨 위 선반에 있어요.
use: I built a shelf for my plants.
Check the shelf life before buying.
mcq: Put the boxes on the shelf.
Put the boxes on the shelves one.
words.note: shelf(단수)-shelves(복수). shelf life = 유통기한, 보너스 표현!

words.ex: This shirt is a bit loose on me.
use: My dog got loose in the park.
mcq: The knot came loose during the hike.
The knot came lose during the hike.
words.note: loose(헐거운/luːs/) vs lose(잃다/luːz/) — 철자·발음 모두 다른 단어!

words.ex: They live on the eastern coast.
use: Eastern Europe has beautiful old cities.
The eastern sky turned orange at dawn.
mcq: We traveled through east-side Canada parts.
words.note: eastern + 지역명. east(동쪽·명사)와 eastern(동쪽의·형용사) 구분!
